posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md:
I would appreciate some advice on what this beam is showing. You can view the video at [http://www.3dimagery.com/671/671.htm](http://www.3dimagery.com/671/671.htm) (5.4MB). The white circle shows the boundary of the microscope objective spreading the beam. 

I have video recorded this first with the room lights on, then off. As you can see, the beam is fluctuating a lot and is definitely not a gaussian profile. I was told this was "near" TEMoo, but I've seen better guassian profiles in interstellar gas photos. 

Does anyone know why the beam is fluctuating (it's working off an expensive power supply with TEC) and why the beam profile is the way it is?

Thank you.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
The fluctuations look to me like noise cause by back reflections. 

The beam quality certainly is dodgy. What kind of laser is that?

btw, why do you use flash animations for your videos? Why not just mpeg's? It makes it impossible to know if one has seen all of the video, or how long it is and you can't pause or replay (without a complete page refresh).

posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md:
I use flash because the file size is half of what a mpeg gives and the quality is much higher. I could introduce controls, but these were made for quick one time viewing, then I'm going to delete them. 

Thanks for the feedback on what you think the fluctuations are.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: That is a useless beam quality. I think Michael is right, it looks like there is a back reflection creating an interference patern. I have seen this when passing diodes through an etalon that is changing temperatures.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: Surely looks like interference. You can see the pattern jump when mode hops happen. Can see similar effects when reflecting a hopping laser diode off a dvd.

posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md:
Thanks for the feed back Michael and Colin. This is a DPSS 671nm laser.

It will make a hologram, but there are curved rings running all through the image. Pretty worthless. Thanks again.

posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md: Whooops, sorry I missed your comment Hans. I thought it also looked like mode hopping. I really appreciate your input. Thanks.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
Steve, aside from the curved rings, how deep was the hologram?

It would be interesting to try to get the temperature under control with a red DPSS as long as the coherence length is good. It should then be possible to eliminate the mode hops.

posts.author: dcgman
posts.content_md:
I think the laser is mostly showing a mixture of TEM00 and TEM01 modes-the modes are described at the following link:

[http://www.mrl.columbia.edu/ntm/level2/ ... 02s07.html](http://www.mrl.columbia.edu/ntm/level2/ch02/html/l2c02s07.html)

As pointed out by others on this forum, it also seems to be jumping between modes.

posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md:
Hans:

The hologram object was only about 3 cm deep. I know absolutely nothing about working on temperature controlling of this laser. I will be in contact next week with the manufacturer to see what can be done to remedy this situation, if anything. Thanks for your feedback on this.

dcgman:

Thank you very much for your input and especially the website showing various modes. Your information adds to what's happening with the beam profile.
